candidate.answerReason: After n pourings, the remaining fraction is 1/(n+1). This equals 1/10 exactly when n=9, agreeing with choice D.

methods.label: Multiply the fractions that remain
methods.explanation:
Track the water that remains after each pouring. Pouring out \(\frac12\) leaves \(\frac12\); pouring out \(\frac13\) of the remainder leaves \(\frac23\) of it; the next pouring leaves \(\frac34\) of what was there.

In general, pouring number \(n\), where \(n\) is a positive integer, leaves \(\frac{n}{n+1}\) of the water present just before that pouring. Thus the fraction of the original water remaining after \(n\) pourings is
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac34\cdots\frac{n}{n+1}
=\frac1{n+1}.
\]
The intermediate numerators and denominators cancel, leaving only the first numerator and the last denominator. All denominators are positive.

For exactly one tenth to remain, we need \(n+1=10\), so \(n=9\). The answer is \(\boxed{9}\) pourings, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
